guideline: CPIC Guideline for CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2B6, SLC6A4, and HTR2A Genotypes and Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Antidepressants (2023 update)

recommendations.text: Select alternative drug not predominantly metabolized by CYP2D6. Increased metabolism of paroxetine to less active compounds; lower plasma concentrations decrease the probability of clinical benefit. Extent of phenoconversion due to paroxetine autoinhibition of CYP2D6 is unclear.
recommendations.citation: CPIC 2023 SRI antidepressant guideline, Table 2a (Bousman et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2023;114(1):51-68; PMID 37032427; doi:10.1002/cpt.2903) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10564324/

recommendations.text: Initiate therapy with recommended starting dose. Paroxetine-associated phenoconversion of normal metabolizers to intermediate or poor metabolizers due to CYP2D6 autoinhibition may occur and is dose-dependent and greater at steady state concentrations.
recommendations.citation: CPIC 2023 SRI antidepressant guideline, Table 2a (Bousman et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2023;114(1):51-68; PMID 37032427) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10564324/

recommendations.text: Consider a lower starting dose and slower titration schedule as compared with normal metabolizers. Reduced metabolism to less active compounds when starting treatment or at lower doses; higher plasma concentrations may increase the probability of side effects.
recommendations.citation: CPIC 2023 SRI antidepressant guideline, Table 2a (Bousman et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2023;114(1):51-68; PMID 37032427) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10564324/

recommendations.text: Consider a 50% reduction in recommended starting dose, slower titration schedule, and a 50% lower maintenance dose as compared with normal metabolizers. Greatly reduced metabolism; higher plasma concentrations may increase the probability of side effects.

recommendations.text: No recommendation due to lack of evidence. No data available for CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizers; insufficient data to assess whether there is a meaningful impact of CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolism on fluvoxamine exposure or clinical outcomes.

notes:
SOURCE VERIFICATION: All Table 2/3/4 rows were extracted verbatim from the CPIC-hosted PDF of the publication (https://files.cpicpgx.org/data/guideline/publication/serotonin_reuptake_inhibitor_antidepressants/2023/37032427.pdf), read directly as text rather than via model summarization. Two independent LLM summarizations of the PMC full text agreed with the PDF on every action and strength value. Citation: Bousman CA, Stevenson JM, Ramsey LB, et al. Clin Pharmacol Ther. 2023;114(1):51-68. PMID 37032427. doi:10.1002/cpt.2903.

SCOPE (verbatim from guideline): "CYP2D6-guided recommendations are made for paroxetine, fluvoxamine, venlafaxine, and vortioxetine; CYP2C19-guided recommendations are made for citalopram, escitalopram, and sertraline; and CYP2B6-guided recommendations are made for sertraline." That is the complete set of dosing tables. 36 of the rows above are true table rows; the remaining 21 encode CPIC's explicit no-impact / no-recommendation statements.

PHENOTYPE COLLAPSING: The CYP2C19 tables include "likely intermediate metabolizer" and "likely poor metabolizer" rows. Their recommendation text and classification are identical to the IM and PM rows respectively, so I collapsed them into Intermediate/Poor with no loss of information. Every table also has an "indeterminate" row = "No recommendation"; the schema has no indeterminate phenotype, so those are omitted — the prototype should treat indeterminate as no_recommendation for all four genes. CYP2D6 tables have no "rapid metabolizer" row (CYP2D6 uses activity score, not an RM category).

IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON action="standard" FOR NOT-AFFECTED DRUGS: CPIC does NOT issue an affirmative "use standard dose" recommendation for these pairs — it assigns either CPIC level C (no recommendation) or no level at all. I coded them "standard" because you asked for enzyme-safety to be machine-readable, and each rests on an explicit narrative statement of no meaningful impact. But the "strength" field for these rows says "No CPIC level assigned" or "CPIC level C" rather than a CPIC strength term, and the text says so. The prototype must not render these as CPIC-endorsed dosing guidance. This is a derived inference from CPIC prose, not a CPIC recommendation.

DRUGS WITH NO CPIC RECOMMENDATION AT ALL (no dosing table for any of the three genes): fluoxetine (CYP2D6, CPIC level C — explicitly stated, encoded above as no_recommendation), duloxetine (CYP2D6, CPIC level C), desvenlafaxine, levomilnacipran, milnacipran, vilazodone (no recommendations and no CPIC levels assigned).

GENE-DRUG PAIRS WHERE CPIC IS SIMPLY SILENT — I deliberately did NOT emit rows, because there is no source statement to cite and inventing "standard" would be fabrication: paroxetine/fluvoxamine/venlafaxine/vortioxetine + CYP2C19; fluoxetine + CYP2C19; duloxetine + CYP2C19 (the no-impact sentence for duloxetine is CYP2D6-specific; duloxetine is a CYP1A2/CYP2D6 substrate and CPIC makes no CYP2C19 claim about it); citalopram/escitalopram + CYP2D6 (CPIC lists citalopram among "major or minor CYP2D6 substrates" with "complex and unclear relationships" — it does NOT say citalopram is CYP2D6-safe, so do not infer enzyme-safety here); and every drug except sertraline + CYP2B6.

SLC6A4 AND HTR2A: no clinical recommendations for any antidepressant. The guideline states evidence is "currently mixed and insufficient to support clinical utility" and assigns CPIC level C (no recommendation) for both genes (Tables S7-S9). These genes should not drive any prototype output.

NOT CAPTURED — TABLE 5 (combined CYP2C19 + CYP2B6 sertraline matrix): the guideline includes a 2-gene matrix that supersedes the single-gene sertraline tables when both genotypes are known. The schema has a single gene field, so I could not encode it. I read the first two rows directly (CYP2C19 UM/RM: standard dose across all CYP2B6 states, classifications Optional/Strong/Moderate/Optional/Strong left-to-right; CYP2C19 NM + CYP2B6 PM begins "Consider a lower starting dose...") but did NOT extract the full matrix, so I am not reporting the rest. If the prototype will ever have both genotypes, Table 5 should be captured in a follow-up pass as a separate two-gene table — using the single-gene rows for a dual-genotype patient will under-call some combinations.

ACTION-ENUM MAPPING JUDGMENTS (mine, not CPIC's): CYP2C19 RM + citalopram/escitalopram coded "increase" because the conditional higher maintenance dose is what distinguishes RM from NM, though the recommendation starts at the standard dose. CYP2C19 IM + citalopram/escitalopram/sertraline coded "decrease" although the starting dose is standard and only titration/maintenance is reduced. CYP2C19 PM + citalopram/escitalopram coded "alternative" since the primary CPIC action is to switch drug, with the 50% reduction as the fallback. Review these mappings before they drive UI logic.
